statics.name: fromJSON
statics.description: Creates a new model from one previously saved as JSON (JavaScript only)

parameters.desc: a JSON string containing the model

functions.name: addText
functions.example:
sample = "One reason people lie is to achieve personal power.";
rm = new RiMarkov(3);
rm.addText(sample);
functions.description: Loads text into the model, first splitting it into sentences (using RiTa.sentences(). If you wish to add an array of sentences directly, use addSentences() instead.

parameters.desc: raw text to be split into sentences and added to the model

functions.name: completions
functions.description:
If only one array parameter is provided, this function returns all possible next words, ordered by probability, for the given array.
 
If two arrays are provided, it returns an unordered array of possible words w that complete the n-gram consisting of: pre[0]...pre[k], w, post[k+1]...post[n].

result = rm.completions([ "the" ], [ "red", "ball" ]);
The line above will return all the single words that occur between 'the' and 'red ball' in the current model (assuming n > 3), eg [ 'round', 'big', 'bouncy' ]).

Note: For this operation to be valid, (pre.length + post.length) must be less than the model's n-factor, otherwise an error will be thrown.

parameters.desc:
options (optional)

{boolean} opts.allowSpecial:
if true, include internal start/end tokens in the results (default=false)

returns.desc: the list of possible next tokens

functions.name: generate
functions.example:
rm = new RiMarkov(3);
rm.addText(sentences);

// Generate one sentence
sent = rm.generate();

// Generate 5 sentences
sents = rm.generate({ numSentences: 5 });

// Generate from a prompt
sent = rm.generate(["the", "cat"]);
functions.description:
Generates one or more sentences from the model.

Supports several call signatures:
generate(n, prompt, opts) — explicit n-gram order, prompt array, options
generate(n, opts)         — n-gram order and options
generate(prompt, opts)    — prompt array and options
generate(opts)            — all parameters in options object

Note: when numSentences > 1, multiple sentences follow the model across sentence boundaries — they are not independent generations.

parameters.desc: n-gram order (optional, uses constructor value if omitted)
prompt — initial tokens to seed the generation (optional)

options (all optional):

{int} options.n:
n-gram order (alternative to positional arg)

{String[]} options.prompt:
prompt tokens (alternative to positional arg)

{int} options.numSentences:
number of sentences to generate, default=1

{int} options.minLength / options.minTokens:
minimum token count before a stop condition is honoured, default=5

{int} options.maxLength / options.maxTokens:
hard cap on tokens generated, default=999

{number} options.temp / options.temperature:
sampling temperature — higher values increase randomness, lower values favor more frequent tokens, zero uses raw probabilities, default=1

{int} options.maxLengthMatch / options.mlm:
maximum run of consecutive tokens that may appear verbatim in the training data, default=∞

{String|Function} options.generateUntil:
a stop token (string) or predicate (token, tokensSoFar) => boolean that ends generation early

{boolean} options.allowSpecial:
if true, include internal start/end tokens in the results (default=false)

{int} options.maxAttempts:
maximum number of attempts to generate a valid sentence before giving up, default=999

{boolean} options.debug / options.dbug:
if true, print debug info to console (default=false)

{boolean} options.forceOriginal:
if true, only generate sequences that appear in the training data

{int} options.topK:
limit sampling to top-K most probable tokens, default=20

{int} options.depth:
maximum depth for generation paths search, default=50

{boolean} options.sortByProb:
if true, sort multi-sentence results by probability

returns.desc: a single string when numSentences=1 (default), otherwise an array of strings

functions.name: probabilities
functions.example:
rm = new RiMarkov(3);
rm.addText(theText);

// next-word distribution after 'the cat'
dist = rm.probabilities(["the", "cat"]);
// -> { sat: 0.5, jumped: 0.3, meowed: 0.2 }

// with temperature
dist = rm.probabilities(["the"], { temp: 1.5 });
functions.description:
Returns the full set of possible next tokens as an object, given an array of tokens as context.

If no tokens are provided, returns the distribution following the implicit start token.
Special start/end tokens are excluded from the result unless options.allowSpecial is set.

parameters.desc:
options (optional)

{number} options.temp:
sampling temperature (default=0, i.e. raw frequencies)

{boolean} options.allowSpecial:
if true, include internal start/end tokens in the result (default=false)

returns.desc: an object mapping possible next tokens to their probabilities, or an empty object if no continuations exist

functions.name: size
functions.description: Returns the number of tokens currently in the model

functions.name: toString
functions.description: Returns a formatted version of this model

functions.name: toJSON
functions.description: Converts the model to a JSON-formatted string  (JavaScript only)

functions.name: stream
functions.example:
rm = new RiMarkov(3);
rm.addText(sentences);

for (const token of rm.stream(["the"])) {
process.stdout.write(token + ' ');
}
functions.description:
A generator that streams tokens one-by-one from the model as they are sampled. Useful for real-time or incremental output.

Supports the same polymorphic call signatures as generate().

parameters.desc: prompt — initial tokens to seed the stream (optional)

options (optional) — same as generate(), with the addition of:

{String|Function} opts.generateUntil:
stop token or predicate (token, tokensSoFar) => boolean, defaults to model's endToken

returns.desc: a generator that yields one token at a time

functions.name: addSentences
functions.example:
rm = new RiMarkov(3);
rm.addSentences(["The cat sat.", "The dog ran."]);
functions.description: Loads an array of pre-split sentences into the model. Each string in the array is treated as an individual sentence (no further splitting is applied). This is the lower-level counterpart to addText().

parameters.desc: an array of sentences to add

functions.name: addTokens
functions.description: Loads a pre-tokenized array of tokens directly into the model, bypassing sentence splitting and tokenization entirely.

parameters.desc: an array of tokens to add
